biography.plain_text: Leon Melchior was a Dutch-born Belgian construction entrepreneur and the founder of Zangersheide, the stud farm and studbook associated with international show jumping. Building hospitals and offices created his fortune; horse breeding became his enduring sporting enterprise. He also chaired and financially supported Maastricht's MVV football club, linking his business success with regional sport.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Zangersheide, entrepreneur Leon Melchior challenged the practice of breeding jumping horses within established regional lines. He studied livestock breeding, combined bloodlines from different countries and assessed the results through sporting performance. When existing registration rules constrained those choices, he established a studbook that gave breeders greater freedom over pairings. Auctions helped connect their young horses with international buyers.

Before developing that enterprise, Melchior had worked as a miner and a contractor's bookkeeper, then started his own construction business with borrowed money. Selling the group in 1972 released capital for later ventures, including investments in DSM and the optical retailer Hans Anders. In his final years, his daughter Judy-Ann assumed Zangersheide's daily management, continuing the breeding programme he had developed.
